
# Experimental Design:

Gastric biopsies from patients with intestinal metaplasia were taken from metaplastic and non-metaplastic control sites. Primary gastric epithelial cells were extracted and expanded on feeder cells and then cultured for few passages as organoid cultures to remove feeder cells. 

DNA was isolated and hybridized to the Illumina EPIC methylation array.

To analyse the generated data in R, we will use and further adapt the "Chip Analysis Methylation Pipeline" (ChAMP) package [Morris J, *et al.*, 2013].

```{r}
fix_myLoad = T
if(fix_myLoad) {
  set.seed(123456789)
  load("../../../../Data/Processed/PolyclonalCultures/DNAm/myLoad_IM_nonIM_and_healthy_stomach_combined_orig_ZZU.RData")
  # for some reason the methylation object has less rows than expected for EPIC arrays while the rgSet object is correct - maybe the wrong annotation was available
  # let's repeat some of the steps done my champ.load to get the full methylation data from EPIC arrays
  # The code is taken almost completely from champ.load, excluding parts that would not be run with the standard settings
  
  detPcut <- 0.01
  SampleCutoff <- 0.1
  ProbeCutoff <- 0
  beadCutoff <- 0.05
  
  mset <- preprocessRaw(myLoad$rgSet)
  detP <- detectionP(myLoad$rgSet)
  tmp = getBeta(mset, "Illumina")
  tmp[detP >= detPcut] <- NA
  message("The fraction of failed positions per sample\n \n            (You may need to delete samples with high proportion of failed probes\n): ")
  numfail <- matrix(colMeans(is.na(tmp)))
  rownames(numfail) <- colnames(detP)
  colnames(numfail) <- "Failed CpG Fraction."
  print(numfail)
  
  RemainSample <- which(numfail < SampleCutoff)
  if (any(numfail >= SampleCutoff)) 
    message("The detSamplecut parameter is : ", SampleCutoff, 
            "\nSamples : ", paste(rownames(numfail)[which(numfail >= 
                                                            SampleCutoff)], collapse = ","), " will be deleted.\n", 
            "There are ", length(RemainSample), " samples left for analysis.\n")
  rgSet <- myLoad$rgSet[, RemainSample]
  detP <- detP[, RemainSample]
  mset <- mset[, RemainSample]
  pd <- myLoad$pd[RemainSample, ]
  tmp <- tmp[, RemainSample]
  
  # Filtering
  mset.f = mset[rowSums(is.na(tmp)) <= ProbeCutoff * 
                  ncol(detP), ]
  message("Filtering probes with a detection p-value above ", 
          detPcut, " in one or more samples has removed ", 
          dim(mset)[1] - dim(mset.f)[1], " probes from the analysis. If a large number of probes have been removed, ChAMP suggests you to identify potentially bad samples.")
  mset = mset.f
  tmp <- tmp[rowSums(is.na(tmp)) <= ProbeCutoff * ncol(detP), ]
  
  
  mybeadcount <- function(x) {
    nb <- getNBeads(x)
    typeIadd <- getProbeInfo(x, type = "I")
    typeImatchA <- match(typeIadd$AddressA, rownames(nb))
    typeImatchB <- match(typeIadd$AddressB, rownames(nb))
    typeIIadd <- getProbeInfo(x, type = "II")
    typeIImatch <- match(typeIIadd$Address, rownames(nb))
    nbcg <- nb
    locusNames <- getManifestInfo(x, "locusNames")
    bc_temp <- matrix(NA_real_, ncol = ncol(x), nrow = length(locusNames), 
                      dimnames = list(locusNames, sampleNames(x)))
    TypeII.Name <- getProbeInfo(x, type = "II")$Name
    bc_temp[TypeII.Name, ] <- nbcg[getProbeInfo(x, type = "II")$AddressA, 
    ]
    TypeI <- getProbeInfo(x, type = "I")
    bcB <- bc_temp
    bcA <- bc_temp
    bcB[TypeI$Name, ] <- nbcg[TypeI$AddressB, ]
    bcA[TypeI$Name, ] <- nbcg[TypeI$AddressA, ]
    bcB3 <- which(bcB < 3)
    bcA3 <- which(bcA < 3)
    bcA2 <- bcA
    bcB2 <- bcB
    bcA2[bcA3] <- NA
    bcA2[bcB3] <- NA
    bc <- data.frame(bcA2)
    bc
  }
  
  # Filter bead counts
  bc = mybeadcount(rgSet)
  bc2 = bc[rowSums(is.na(bc)) < beadCutoff * (ncol(bc)), ]
  mset.f2 = mset[featureNames(mset) %in% row.names(bc2), ]
  tmp <- tmp[rownames(tmp) %in% row.names(bc2), ]
  message("Filtering probes with a beadcount <3 in at least ", 
          beadCutoff * 100, "% of samples, has removed ", 
          dim(mset)[1] - dim(mset.f2)[1], " from the analysis.")
  mset = mset.f2
  
  # Filter non-CG
  mset.f2 = dropMethylationLoci(mset, dropCH = T)
  tmp <- tmp[rownames(tmp) %in% featureNames(mset.f2), ]
  message("Filtering non-cg probes, has removed ", 
          dim(mset)[1] - dim(mset.f2)[1], " from the analysis.")
  mset <- mset.f2
  
  # SNP filtering
  message("Using general EPIC SNP list for filtering.")
  data(EPIC.manifest.hg19)
  maskname <- rownames(EPIC.manifest.hg19)[which(EPIC.manifest.hg19$MASK_general == TRUE)]
  mset.f2 = mset[!featureNames(mset) %in% maskname, ]
  tmp <- tmp[!rownames(tmp) %in% maskname, ]
  message("Filtering probes with SNPs as identified in Zhou's Nucleic Acids Research Paper, 2016, has removed ", 
          dim(mset)[1] - dim(mset.f2)[1], " from the analysis.")
  mset = mset.f2
  
  # Filter Multi-hit
  data(multi.hit)
  mset.f2 = mset[!featureNames(mset) %in% multi.hit$TargetID, ]
  tmp <- tmp[!rownames(tmp) %in% multi.hit$TargetID, ]
  message("Filtering probes that align to multiple locations as identified in Nordlund et al, has removed ", 
          dim(mset)[1] - dim(mset.f2)[1], " from the analysis.")
  mset = mset.f2
  
  # Filter X/Y probes
  data(probe.features.epic)
  autosomes = probe.features[!probe.features$CHR %in% 
                               c("X", "Y"), ]
  mset.f2 = mset[featureNames(mset) %in% row.names(autosomes), ]
  tmp <- tmp[rownames(tmp) %in% row.names(autosomes), ]
  message("Filtering probes on the X or Y chromosome has removed ", 
          dim(mset)[1] - dim(mset.f2)[1], " from the analysis.")
  mset = mset.f2
  
  beta.raw <- tmp
  intensity <- minfi::getMeth(mset) + minfi::getUnmeth(mset)
  detP <- detP[which(row.names(detP) %in% row.names(beta.raw)), ]
  
  if (min(beta.raw, na.rm = TRUE) <= 0) 
    beta.raw[beta.raw <= 0] <- min(beta.raw[beta.raw > 
                                              0])
  message("Zeros in your dataset have been replaced with smallest positive value.\n")
  if (max(beta.raw, na.rm = TRUE) >= 0) 
    beta.raw[beta.raw >= 1] <- max(beta.raw[beta.raw < 
                                              1])
  message("One in your dataset have been replaced with largest value below 1.\n")
  
  message("The analysis will be proceed with ", dim(beta.raw)[1], 
          " probes and ", dim(beta.raw)[2], " samples.\n")
  message("Current Data Set contains ", sum(is.na(beta.raw)), 
          " NA in ", "[Beta]", " Matrix.\n")
  
  pd$PatientID <- ifelse(pd$Project=="ZZU", paste0("P_", gsub("IM|NON IM|A|AC|C","",pd$Sample_Name)), pd$PatientID)
  
  myLoad <- list(mset = mset, rgSet = rgSet, pd = pd, intensity = intensity, 
                 beta = beta.raw, detP = detP)
  
  save(myLoad, file=file.path(data_storage_folder, "myLoad_IM_nonIM_and_healthy_stomach_combined.RData"), compress = T)
}
```

# Data Import

Raw intensity values (red and green channel .idat files) are loaded and transformed as beta values. In this process, some filtering steps are already included:
Probes   
- with a detection p-value > 0.01  
- with a bead-count < 3  
- in which the probed CpG falls near a SNP as defined in Zhou W. *et al.*, 2016  
- in which the probe aligns to multiple locations with bwa as defined in Nordlund *et al.*, 2013   
and   
- non-cg probes  
are removed.

# Quality Control raw data

The QC function uses the raw beta values for initial quality control:  
- The Multidimensional Scaling Plot (MDS) visualizes the similarity of the samples based on the    top 1,000 most variable probes of all samples.  
- The density Plot displays the beta distribution of each sample  
- The dendrogram clusters all samples (the distance between the samples is calculated directly by   all probes)  


```{r QC raw}
champ.QC()
```


# Normalization

The normlization method applied here is "SWAN (subset-quantile within array normalization)" [Maksimovic J, *et al.*, 2012], which adjusts for the type I and type II bias of the methylation array. 

```{r Normalization} 
if(rerun_preprocessing){
  myNorm = champ.norm(method = "SWAN", arraytype = "EPIC")
  ed <- myLoad$pd
  save(myNorm, ed, file = file.path(data_storage_folder,"myNorm_IM_nonIM_and_healthy_stomach.RData"), compress=T)
} else {
  load(file.path(data_storage_folder, "myNorm_IM_nonIM_and_healthy_stomach.RData"))
}

```

# Quality Control normalized Data  

## MDS plot

The Multidimensional Scaling Plot (MDS) visualizes the similarity of the samples based on the top 1,000 most variable probes of all samples.


```{r}
## modify mdsPlot function to not show the legend

my_mdsPlot = function (dat, numPositions = 1000, sampNames = NULL, sampGroups = NULL, 
          xlim, ylim, pch = 1, pal = brewer.pal(8, "Dark2"), legendPos = "bottomleft", 
          legendNCol, main = NULL) 
{
  if (is(dat, "MethylSet") || is(dat, "RGChannelSet")) {
    b <- getBeta(dat)
    if (is.null(main)) 
      main <- sprintf("Beta MDS\n%d most variable positions", 
                      numPositions)
  }
  else if (is(dat, "matrix")) {
    b <- dat
    if (is.null(main)) 
      main <- sprintf("MDS\n%d most variable positions", 
                      numPositions)
  }
  else {
    stop("dat must be an 'MethylSet' or 'matrix'.")
  }
  o <- order(-matrixStats::rowVars(b))[1:numPositions]
  d <- dist(t(b[o, ]))
  fit <- cmdscale(d)
  if (missing(xlim)) 
    xlim <- range(fit[, 1]) * 1.2
  if (missing(ylim)) 
    ylim <- range(fit[, 2]) * 1.2
  if (is.null(sampGroups)) 
    sampGroups <- rep(1, numPositions)
  sampGroups <- as.factor(sampGroups)
  col <- pal[sampGroups]
  if (is.null(sampNames)) {
    plot(fit[, 1], fit[, 2], col = col, pch = pch, xlim = xlim, 
         ylim = ylim, xlab = "First dimension", ylab = "Second dimension", main = main, cex.axis = 0.8, cex.lab = 0.8)
  }
  else {
    plot(0, 0, type = "n", xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim, xlab = "First dimension", 
         ylab = "Second dimension", main = main, cex.axis = 0.8, cex.lab = 0.8)
    text(fit[, 1], fit[, 2], sampNames, col = col)
  }
}

```


```{r MDS plot, fig.width=6, fig.height=5}

mdsPlot(myNorm, numPositions = 1000, sampGroups = myLoad$pd$Sample_Group, sampNames = myLoad$pd$Sample_Name, legendPos = "topleft")
```

## Density Plot  
The density Plot displays the beta distribution of each sample.

```{r density plot}

densityPlot(dat = myNorm, sampGroups = myLoad$pd$Sample_Group, main = paste("Density plot of normalized data (", nrow(myNorm), " probes)", sep = ""))

densityPlot(dat = myNorm, sampGroups = myLoad$pd$PatientID, main = paste("Density plot of normalized data (", nrow(myNorm), " probes)", sep = ""))
```

## Dendrogram  

The dendrogram clusters all samples (the distance between the samples is calculated directly by all probes)

```{r dendrogram}

hc <- hclust(dist(t(myNorm)))
dend <- as.dendrogram(hc)
MyColor <- rainbow(length(table(myLoad$pd$Sample_Group)))
names(MyColor) <- names(table(myLoad$pd$Sample_Group))
labels_colors(dend) <- MyColor[myLoad$pd$Sample_Group[order.dendrogram(dend)]]
dend <- dend %>% set("labels_cex", 0.7)
dend <- dend %>% set("leaves_pch", 19) %>% set("leaves_cex", 0.6) %>% set("leaves_col",         MyColor[myLoad$pd$Sample_Group[order.dendrogram(dend)]])
plot(dend, center = TRUE, main = paste("All samples (", nrow(myNorm), " probes)", sep = ""))
legend("topright", fill = MyColor, legend = names(MyColor))


hc <- hclust(dist(t(myNorm)))
dend <- as.dendrogram(hc)
MyColor <- rainbow(length(table(myLoad$pd$PatientID)))
names(MyColor) <- names(table(myLoad$pd$PatientID))
labels_colors(dend) <- MyColor[myLoad$pd$PatientID[order.dendrogram(dend)]]
dend <- dend %>% set("labels_cex", 0.7)
dend <- dend %>% set("leaves_pch", 19) %>% set("leaves_cex", 0.6) %>% set("leaves_col",         MyColor[as.character(myLoad$pd$PatientID[order.dendrogram(dend)])])
plot(dend, center = TRUE, main = paste("All samples (", nrow(myNorm), " probes)", sep = ""))
legend("topright", fill = MyColor, legend = names(MyColor))

```

## Heatmap  

The Heatmap visualizes the similarity of the samples based on the top 1,000 most variable probes of all samples.

```{r heatmap 1000 most var}
o <- order(-matrixStats::rowVars(myNorm))[1:1000]
data <- myNorm[o,]
col_anno <- as.data.frame(myLoad$pd)[,c("Sample_Group", "PatientID")]
pheatmap(data, cluster_rows = T, main = "Heatmap of 1,000 most variable CpGs", show_rownames = FALSE, annotation_col = col_anno, fontsize_col = 8, labels_col = myLoad$pd[colnames(data),"Sample_Name"])
```

# Batch effect correction

With the ChAMP SVD function (runs Singular Value Decomposition on a dataset to estimate the impact of batch effects) I test for putative batch effects.

<!-- and perform subsequently batch effect correction using the champ.runCombat method for batch adjustment, adjusting for the slide, which at the same time adjusts for the patient effect as well, because each patient was hybridized to a different slide. -->

The first plot shows the result of the SVD analysis before adjustment. Then the data are adjusted for "slide". And the second plots shows the result of the SVD analysis after adjustment.

```{r, message=FALSE}

champ.SVD(RGEffect = TRUE, beta = myNorm )
```
